💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, gear-obsessed editors choose every product we review.
  • Portable power stations are handy for backup power during outages, off-grid electricity for an RV, or simply charging your laptop and phone while working remotely.
  • It has been revealed that portable power stations come in a broad range of sizes from brands like Jackery and EcoFlow, including smaller models capable of charging a few devices and high-capacity backup units to keep your lighting and critical appliances on during a days-long blackout.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, gear-obsessed editors choose every product we review. We may earn commission if you buy from a link. Why Trust Us?

Portable power stations are handy for backup power during outages, off-grid electricity for an RV, or simply charging your laptop and phone while working remotely. They’re effectively large bundles of rechargeable lithium-ion batteries, which provide a quiet, exhaust-free alternative to noisy gas-powered portable generators.

It has been revealed that portable power stations come in a broad range of sizes from brands like Jackery and EcoFlow, including smaller models capable of charging a few devices and high-capacity backup units to keep your lighting and critical appliances on during a days-long blackout. Plus, most can be recharged using solar panels.

In a recent development, we evaluated eight power stations of varying sizes, focusing on each model’s maximum output, capacity, charging time, and portability. To test max output, we connected enough electronics and appliances to each power station to meet or slightly exceed its listed max output to see how well it could operate at maximum load. We then tested capacity, using an electricity usage monitor to record the total watt-hours each power station produced while running them under a consistent load.

Once they were drained, we charged each power station from 0 to 100 percent using its AC adapter, timing how long it took to get to 80 and 100 percent capacity. Finally, we evaluated each power station’s portability by attempting to carry it or roll it. Other factors that weighed into our decisions included the number and power output of each power station’s inputs and its charging options.

Our test team for this article includes David Dritsas, an editor who covers generators, lawn and garden, and more; Bradley Ford, an editor with more than five years of experience testing and writing about generators, generator maintenance, power tools, and lawn and garden equipment; and Tony Carrick, a frequent Popular Mechanics contributor who covers landscaping, home improvement, gardening, and home security.

Sources indicate that bluetti manages to pack a lot of power into the Elite 200 V2. It has a max output of 2,600 watts (with 3,900-watt startup power) and a 2,073.6-watt-hour capacity, all while being relatively compact.

We hooked up a miter saw, blender, and space heater, all three of which it powered simultaneously. It easily handled the spike to 4,000 watts to start up the saw, above its listed 3,900-watt starting power, before maintaining an even flow of around 2,500 watts.

The Elite 200 V2 also impressed with the quality of its battery. We recorded 92 percent of its listed 2,073.6-watt-hour capacity, well over the 85 percent average for most portable power stations. It has a quick recharge time for its capacity, going from 0 to 80 percent in 81 minutes and to full in just 107 minutes. And because it uses a LiFePO4 battery, it discharges and recharges for 6,000 cycles before it drops below 80 percent capacity.

According to recent reports, the Elite 200 V2 gives you plenty of output and input options for its size, too. Four AC outlets allow you to load up multiple appliances. There are four USB ports for charging smaller devices, a car accessory outlet, and a DC output. Along with its power cord, there’s a port for charging from a car accessory port or with up to 1,000 watts of solar panels.

With a great power-to-weight ratio, the latest version of the Bluetti Elite 200 V2 is a great portable power station for powering a camper or providing backup power for the essentials.

A fresh and improved version of Jackery’s extremely popular Explorer 1000, the Explorer 1000 V2 features a slightly larger storage capacity, up 70 watt-hours, and a much higher 1,500-watt output—a 50 percent jump from 1,000 watts of the original. This allows you to power devices with higher loads, like an electric grill or a large microwave. Jackery managed this while maintaining the Explorer 1000’s compact size and weight, so it’s still easy to carry with you on a camping trip.

The Explorer 1000 V2 features three standard 120-volt AC outlets, two USB-C ports (30- and 100-watt), one USB-A port (18-watt), and one 12-volt DC outlet. Paired with Jackery’s app, you can monitor the power station locally via Bluetooth or from anywhere when it’s connected via WiFi. The app allows for checking charge levels and estimated run time, as well as toggling any of the outputs on or off. Plugged into the wall, the power station charges in under two hours. It’s also possible to charge it from your vehicle in up to 12 hours.

In a recent development, performance-wise, the 1000 V2 did well powering a 25-cubic-foot refrigerator for 18 hours and 22 minutes, which is better performance than we’ve gotten from other tested 1000-watt models. Under a constant load of 475 watts (that’s a little less than a small coffee maker), it ran for 1 hour and 57 minutes.

According to recent reports, this power station offers a lot of bang for the buck. Sure, it isn’t going to power your house through a days-long outage, but it offers a lot of nice features for the price, making it one of the better values out there, especially if you pick it up on sale.

What is most impressive about the Anker S2000 power station is its ability to maximize its runtime. During our testing, we were able to run a full-sized refrigerator for just over 24 hours, which is nearly six hours longer than other power stations we’ve tested with comparable capacity.

Sources indicate that it does this using a technology that recognizes the type of device plugged in and adjusts the inverter's frequency to match the type of demand. This, in theory, helps reduce the amount of wasted power. From what we can tell, it works very well.

Recent findings suggest that the S2000 is fairly well equipped, too, with five outlets for AC power (two are in the back) and a bank of USB ports for home use, and can operate as an uninterruptible power supply (UPS) for 10-millisecond automated backup. With only 1,500 watts of output, it may struggle with some high-power appliances like a large microwave, but for many people, this station can deliver power during a blackout and keep you up and running for a long time.

Recent findings suggest that one of the standout features of Bluetti’s Apex 200 is a maximum solar input of up to 3,000 watts. You rarely find that much input power for a station of this size. There are two sets of DC inputs for this: low-voltage XT60 input (up to 1,000 watts) and high-voltage MC4 input (up to 2,000 watts). If you have the panels and enough perfect direct sunlight to achieve this full potential, you could fully charge this station in less than two hours using the sun’s rays.

In a recent development, beyond that, the Apex 200 is a fairly robust power station, with 3,200 watts of continuous power. (It notes 3,600 on the front, but that’s only if it’s connected to an expansion battery.) I ran my refrigerator for a full 27 hours on a single charge, and when I tested it for battery efficiency, I estimated it at about 90 percent, which is very good for a power station. There’s also a 120-volt 30-amp output if you wanted to run a few circuits in your home by hooking up to a manual transfer switch. Just keep in mind that there’s no 240-volt support, so you can’t use it to power high-voltage appliances like electric dryers.

The 2,560-watt-hour battery capacity isn't huge—at least not for home backup—but you can expand it by adding up to six additional batteries. That could add up to over 33 kilowatt-hours if you use the largest batteries Bluetti offers, the B500K. That’s massive.

According to recent reports, even with all this power, the Apex 200 is still a fairly portable station. Weighing 59 pounds, it’s not too hard to move around the house or in and out of a vehicle. So, when you’re not using it for home backup, it’s perfect for taking on a long outdoor trip or for powering an RV when a site hookup is not available.

Full Bluetti Apex 200 Power Station Review.

Industry observers note that this is one of the most rugged power stations we’ve seen yet. The Jackery Explorer 1500 Ultra features an IP65 weatherproof rating, molded rubber port covers, a shockproof enclosure, and a bottom drainage system and cooling structure that help keep water out of the enclosure. All work together to resist the elements better than most power stations can.

Recent findings suggest that the unique cooling system was particularly interesting. A titanium alloy plate within the structure helps dissipate heat without the need for multiple fans and eliminates the need for any side vents (typical in most power stations) that could allow droplets of water in. Meanwhile, you can remove an external plate on the bottom and dry it if water does make its way in.

In a recent development, the 1,800 watts of output power and 1,536 watt-hours of battery capacity are decent if you’re taking this camping for the weekend and need to recharge devices, run a low-powered small appliance or two, and plug in some lighting. But don’t expect to run something like a space heater for very long, though.

Full Jackery Explorer 1500 Ultra Power Station Review.

Recent findings suggest that the S5000 is the second power station in Anker's S-series, which features inverter efficiency technology that helps to reduce wasted energy when the inverter is idling or running lower-powered devices. We were impressed with how this technology performed in the S2000, and this model matched that performance.

We ran this through several tests, and the battery efficiency proved to be around 97 percent (the industry average is around 89 percent). For example, we left the AC inverter idling for 18 hours, and the battery remained at 100 percent capacity. Meanwhile, another station we idled at the same time lost 19 percent of its available power. That was impressive.

Sources indicate that the next most impressive attribute about the S5000 is its size. It’s at least half the size of other power stations that feature 5,000 watt-hours of capacity and includes just as many outputs, including a 240-volt, 30-amp outlet. It also has both high- and low-powered DC inputs that enable up to 3,000 watts of solar power input if you have the panels to generate that. You can also recharge at up to 4,500 watts using a direct DC connection to Anker's 5500 Smart Tri-Fuel generator.

With only 4,500 watts of total output, we wouldn’t call this a contender for true whole-home backup (Anker’s E-10 system is a better option for that), but the S5000 can deliver a decent amount to power an RV, run lights and appliances during an emergency, or even a couple of critical circuits.

During our hands-on test, Goal Zero’s newest Yeti 1500 impressed us with its capable performance and sturdy construction. It’s the replacement for an older model and improves on its predecessor with improved weatherproofing, more outputs, and a better battery.

This 2,000-watt power station is clearly designed for outdoor use with an IPX4 water-resistance rating and new outlet shields that cover the ports and inputs when you’re not using them. That’s great for dusty conditions. Each section is nicely illuminated by an LED light and can be individually turned on/off using a manual button or the mobile app (and will shut off if not used after a duration of time). These additions make it perfect for camping or other outdoor uses. You can’t leave it out in the rain, but getting a bit of water on it won’t be a concern.

We loved the increased number of outputs on the Yeti 1500. There are now four 120-volt AC outlets and six USB ports: four USB-C (two are high-powered) and two USB-A ports, plus four 12-volt connections (though two of those are proprietary for Goal Zero accessories and not all that useful in our estimation). There are also inputs for AC power, 12-volt DC, and inputs for both low- and high-voltage solar power that can be used simultaneously. Theoretically, you could recharge this station with up to 900 watts of eco-friendly electrical current.

It has been revealed that as part of our test, we simulated a blackout at home and managed to run a cable modem/Wi-Fi router, a lamp, a TV, and a tower fan, while simultaneously charging a phone and a laptop through the USB-C ports. Given the station’s output and capacity, there was enough power for over two days of use (conveniently shown on the main display), and there was plenty of room to spare for a few more devices.

Sources indicate that the mobile app was easy to use and chock-full of great information on energy consumption. The only problem we had was maintaining a stable Bluetooth connection. It needed to be manually paired every time we went to use it, which was annoying. Wi-Fi is available, but that’s not so useful when you are off-grid.

Industry observers note that we should warn you that the Yeti 1500 is heavy at 53 pounds. If you’re taking it on a trip, you’ll need a bit of strength to lug it around. That aside, the 2026 Yeti 1500 is a well-designed power station that’s ideal for off-grid camping, especially when there are dusty or wet conditions. We’d happily take it on our next camping trip.

Full Goal Zero Yeti 1500 Review.

Industry observers note that though it’s no longer EcoFlow’s flagship backup power solution, the original Delta Pro is still a massive power station with a good amount of electrical output. The brand claims it powers nearly any appliance, and after testing, we’re inclined to agree. With an output of 3,600 watts, it can handle multiple appliances, and it’s possible to bump the output to 4,500 watts with its built-in X-Boost technology if you need more power.

Sources indicate that in testing, we ran it with a continuous 470-watt load for 6 hours and 57 minutes, as indicated on the Delta Pro’s display. Of course, in a home backup during a power outage situation, we would run only the bare essentials to conserve power. To that end, we used it to power a full-size, 25-cubic-foot refrigerator, which it did for a remarkable 51 hours and 24 minutes.

Recharging the power station from empty using a standard 120-volt home outlet, it recharged to full capacity in 2 hours and 36 minutes. There’s also an included adapter for charging the system at EV charging stations, with solar panels (sold separately), with a car charger, or combinations of these to speed things up.

The Delta Pro’s display screen provides all the crucial information you need to manage your power consumption. We frequently checked the screen during testing to see the unit’s charge level, current load, and estimated run time at the current discharge rate.

All of this information is accessible through EcoFlow’s app, which was the most intuitive and easiest to use of those tested. We connected the app both locally using Bluetooth and remotely via WiFi to monitor the power station from anywhere. We could also toggle outlets on and off remotely, which is helpful if you’re trying to manage power station output to extend the battery life.

Industry observers note that we’ve tested the brand’s Whole-Home Backup Kit, which includes two of the power stations and a dual-voltage hub used to connect to your home service panel via a transfer switch. We used this setup to power critical circuits in a Northeast Pennsylvania home in late winter.

The Delta Pro Whole Home Kit ran just over 24 hours, powering kitchen outlets, a full-size refrigerator, a chest freezer, a cable modem and wireless network, and a hot water boiler. Plus, having charged these two Delta Pro power stations previously, we found that they were able to hold a full charge for a full eight months.

Testing was performed under normal usage conditions—run time could easily be extended by employing standard power-conservation strategies like lowering the thermostat, powering the fridge and freezer for four hours on and four hours off, and only opening them when absolutely necessary.

EcoFlow’s Delta Pro Whole Home Kit is a legitimate home backup system that can operate inside your home, with none of the risks or potential hassles of running a generator, such as dangerous carbon monoxide gas from exhaust fumes and dealing with fuel and oil.

A portable power station’s maximum output tells you the total watts it can produce, which determines what you can and can’t power with it. Look for a power station that can handle the combined wattage of the electronics you plan to plug into it.

Recent findings suggest that some power stations also have surge power that allows them to produce higher wattage for short bursts. This is designed specifically for appliances that draw more watts (known as starting watts) in the first few seconds when you first start them up, including power tools, refrigerators, blenders, and window air conditioners.

According to recent reports, A portable power station’s capacity, listed in watt-hours (Wh), determines how much energy a power station can deliver over time. Generally, power stations with more watt-hours can run for longer, but exactly how long depends on the amount of watts the devices connected to the power station draw. You can roughly estimate how long a power station will last by dividing the total watt-hours by the watts drawn (Wh ÷ W = Hrs).

For example, if you have a power station with 2,048-watt-hour capacity and are consistently drawing 400 watts of power: 2,048 ÷ 400 = 5.12 hours of runtime.

Keep in mind that the usable watt-hours are not the same as the watt-hours listed on the power station’s label. You’ll typically get about 85 percent of the listed watt-hours due to power lost in connections and the electricity that the power station itself uses to power its inverter and display. Given those losses, expect to get about 85 percent of a power station’s listed watt-hours in usable power. So, a fully charged 2,000-watt-hour power station will typically give you about 1,700 watt-hours of usable power.

These days, most portable power stations, including all those we recommend here, use LiFePO4 batteries, which are capable of holding far more cycles, which is the number of times a battery goes through a complete discharge and recharge, than older lithium-ion batteries, while also being less likely to combust. Their one drawback is that they have a lower energy density, which means it takes more LiFePO4 batteries than lithium-ion batteries to produce the same amount of power. Still, this is the battery type of choice for portable power stations, both large and small.

While all these power stations are portable, some are easier to transport than others. A power station’s portability is directly related to its power capacity and output.

Small power stations with around 300 watt-hours of capacity and a max output of 300 watts typically weigh under 10 pounds and are about the size of a lunch box.

Midsize models like the Bluetti Elite 200 V2 portable power station, which have a max wattage of between 2,000 and 2,600 watts and a 2,000-watt-hour capacity, are about the size of the printer in your home office and weigh around 60 pounds, just small and light enough for one person to carry from one room to another.

Recent findings suggest that large portable models can weigh up to 135 pounds and are about the size of a suitcase. While these monsters are too large for one person to lift, they do sit on wheels that allow you to move them over flat surfaces, technically making them portable.

In a recent development, portable power stations have an array of output ports, including USB-C, USB-A, car accessory, AC, and RV. Consider what types of appliances or electronics you’re planning to charge and the type of connections they use when choosing a portable power station.

Sources indicate that since the wattage of the output can vary, also consider the maximum charging output of each port to avoid disappointing recharge times. For example, a power station with a USB-C port that has a 15-watt max output will take a much longer time to charge a laptop than one with a 140-watt USB-C port.

If you’re looking for a large-capacity power station that will back up critical circuits in your home or power an RV, you’ll need a station that features a single 30-amp connection that can connect to an RV input or transfer switch.

Portable power stations have control panels with LED displays and buttons that turn inputs off and on and display usage and remaining power. Most portable power stations are also compatible with Bluetooth and Wi-Fi, allowing you to monitor and control them remotely from a smartphone app.

Often, what makes a power station great is the kind of software it includes and what features it offers to help you best manage your power station. For example, some stations that you leave plugged into a wall—so that they stay charged and at the ready—will automatically only recharge your station during low-peak hours when rates may be lower from your electric utility. Features like this one can be incredibly helpful when trying to get the most from your station.

Most large power stations, including the EcoFlow Delta 3 Plus and Anker F3800 Plus, can serve as a UPS (uninterruptible power supply) for your home. To use these power stations as a UPS, plug them into the wall, then plug whatever devices you want backed up into the station’s AC output ports. When the power is on, those devices use energy from the grid. When there is a power outage, the power station instantly switches these devices to battery power. If you live in an area prone to power outages, this can be useful to prevent data loss from a connected computer, keep medical devices running, or run the pump and filter on a fish tank.

Portable power stations heat up when operating for extended periods or when they’re providing power for multiple devices. Internal fans will kick on to keep the power station from overheating. While these fans are far quieter than the roar of a gas-powered generator, they do still create some noise. Smaller power stations are about as loud as a small fan, while larger ones produce about the same amount of noise as a refrigerator.

Recent findings suggest that A portable power station’s lifespan depends on the type of battery inside. Most upcoming portable power stations, including all the models we recommend here, feature LiFePO4 battery technology, which lasts far longer than older lithium-ion technology.

Sources indicate that how much more? LiFePO4 power stations will last for more than 3,000 charge cycles, or about 10 years. That’s far longer than the 500 or so charge cycles and 3 to 5 years you’ll get from an older power station with a lithium-ion battery.

That depends on the capacity of your portable power station, the wattage of your solar panels, and the weather. To figure that out, divide the station’s total capacity by the total input power of the solar panels (Wh ÷ W = Hrs).

It has been revealed that for example, a 1,000-watt-hour power station that’s receiving a consistent stream of 200 watts of power from a solar panel would take about 5 hours to recharge. Keep in mind, this is assuming uninterrupted, direct sunlight conditions, which, even then, may produce varied results.

Some power stations have ingress protection (IP) ratings, indicating they have been tested for water and dust resistance. The Bluetti Elite 200, for example, has an IP65 rating, which means it can withstand water sprays from all angles. However, other portable power stations do not have a weather rating, so it’s vital to check if you proposal on using your power station outdoors. Regardless, it’s a good idea to protect your power station from any water or severe weather conditions as much as possible.

Which Thanksgiving Foods Belong in the Same Bite?

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (798 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Tasteofhome

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that some Thanksgiving food combinations are obvious.
  • For years, my kids refused to let any two foods touch on their plates.
  • Of course, plenty of adults also have strong opinions about which Thanksgiving foods should mingle.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Taste of Home's Editorial Process.

Industry observers note that some Thanksgiving food combinations are obvious. Others might earn you some questioning looks at the dinner table.

For years, my kids refused to let any two foods touch on their plates. I found this particularly maddening at Thanksgiving. There’s an entire table of food to fit onto a single plate and only so much room to negotiate separate territories for the mashed potatoes and green bean casserole! Thankfully, they’re a little more accommodating these days and, like me, have come to appreciate the occasional overlap between dishes.

Of course, plenty of adults also have strong opinions about which Thanksgiving foods should mingle. There are those who insist on keeping every dish separate, those who permit a little gravy to stray onto the stuffing but draw the line at cranberry sauce, and those who deliberately assemble the perfect combination on every forkful. Then there’s always the unhinged relative who stirs the entire contents of their plate into a single, gravy-saturated mass and eats it with the serene confidence of someone who has never once questioned their choices.

Sources indicate that personally, I’m firmly in favor of combining foods, although I do believe a little discretion is in order. Thanksgiving dinner offers a wonderful assortment of rich, savory and tart flavors, and knowing which ones to bring together is part of what makes the meal so satisfying. There’s a culinary reason that cranberry sauce belongs alongside turkey, and that stuffing and mashed potatoes are particularly good together. And once you understand why those combinations work, you can start building some excellent bites of your own.

Recent findings suggest that absolutely. In fact, some of the most familiar food pairings are built around the idea that one ingredient can supply something another lacks. Think of a rich cut of meat served with a sharp, acidic sauce, or a creamy dish finished with something crisp. Neither component is necessarily lacking on its own, but the contrast makes the combination much more interesting.

Sources indicate that the same principle applies to Thanksgiving foods. Acidity helps balance richness, sweetness can temper salty or intensely savory flavors, and a change in texture can make a forkful more interesting. It’s not particularly complicated, but there’s a difference between understanding why two foods complement each other and simply hoping for the best.

Some combinations are simply better than others, though saying so at Thanksgiving dinner may invite more opinions than you bargained for.

Turkey and cranberry sauce: There’s a reason this pairing has endured for generations. Turkey, particularly the breast meat, is relatively mild, and the tartness of cranberry sauce gives it a welcome lift. It’s also an excellent remedy for turkey that’s spent a little too long in the oven, a situation that has befallen even the most conscientious Thanksgiving cooks.

Recent findings suggest that mashed potatoes, stuffing and gravy: I consider this one of Thanksgiving’s greatest achievements. The smooth, buttery potatoes and herbaceous stuffing are excellent together, and a generous spoonful of gravy makes the whole arrangement even better. There’s nothing particularly subtle about it, but Thanksgiving dinner isn’t generally celebrated for its subtlety.

Industry observers note that sweet potatoes and turkey: The natural sweetness of roasted sweet potatoes makes a lovely contrast to savory turkey, particularly the richer dark meat. A traditional sweet potato casserole can work, too, although I draw the line somewhere around the marshmallow topping. I have nothing against marshmallows, but I prefer to encounter them after dinner.

Green bean casserole and mashed potatoes: These are two of my Thanksgiving essentials, and I see no reason they shouldn’t share a fork. The creamy green beans and buttery potatoes are lovely together, but it’s the crispy fried onions that really make the combination work. That salty crunch is a welcome addition to the softer textures.

Recent findings suggest that turkey, stuffing and cranberry sauce: This is probably my favorite combo of the bunch. The savory turkey and seasoned stuffing are practically made for one another, while a little cranberry sauce cuts through the richness. It’s essentially a Thanksgiving leftover sandwich without the bread, although I wouldn’t object to adding a dinner roll to the equation.

In a recent development, macaroni and cheese and cranberry sauce: I realize this combination may call my culinary credentials into question, but hear me out. Rich, creamy mac and cheese practically begs for something sharp and acidic to cut through it, and cranberry sauce does exactly that. It’s not so different from serving a sharp cheddar with fruit preserves on a charcuterie board, although I concede that putting cranberry sauce on macaroni and cheese is a considerably harder sell. But that’s half the fun of Thanksgiving dinner: discovering which combinations you’re willing to defend.

Recent findings suggest that one of the latest innovations catching our attention? Hybrid bakeware. This emerging category puts a latest spin on traditional baking pans, combining some of the best features of different materials.

So what exactly is hybrid bakeware, and is it worth the kitchen upgrade? Let’s take a closer look.

According to recent reports, traditional bakeware usually features one primary material, such as aluminum, stainless steel or glass. Hybrid bakeware, on the other hand, takes a different approach by pairing multiple materials together. For example, durable stainless steel pairs with an easy-release ceramic nonstick coating. You get the best of both worlds in one pan.

Recent findings suggest that stainless steel and ceramic nonstick make a pretty dynamic duo in baking. Stainless steel delivers durability and provides a sturdy baking surface, while nonstick helps prevent baked goods from sticking to the pan.

Breaking: Jim Jordan picked as fresh minority leader for House GOP

📅 10 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1213 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rollcall

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Jim Jordan, R-Ohio, center, arrives for a House Republican leadership candidate forum for the 120th Congress in the Capitol Visitor Center on Tuesday, with Rep.
  • Sources indicate that house Republicans on Tuesday opted for a new face atop their ranks, electing Rep.
  • The Ohio Republican defeated outgoing Majority Leader Steve Scalise, R-La., in a closed-door, secret-ballot election.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, rep. Jim Jordan, R-Ohio, center, arrives for a House Republican leadership candidate forum for the 120th Congress in the Capitol Visitor Center on Tuesday, with Rep. Celeste Maloy, R-Utah, walking alongside him. (Bill Clark/CQ Roll Call).

Sources indicate that house Republicans on Tuesday opted for a new face atop their ranks, electing Rep. Jim Jordan as the incoming minority leader for the 120th Congress after Republicans suffered massive losses in last week’s midterm elections.

The Ohio Republican defeated outgoing Majority Leader Steve Scalise, R-La., in a closed-door, secret-ballot election. The final tally was 106-73.

“Over the next two years, House Republicans will fight for American families. Democrats offer more government. We will offer more freedom,” Jordan mentioned after the hourslong process.

Recent findings suggest that the two had been working the phones before making their pitches during a candidates forum in the Capitol Visitor Center’s auditorium on Tuesday morning. Speaker Mike Johnson, R-La., announced last week he would not seek a leadership post in the new Congress, which will be seated on Jan. 3.

“Obviously Jim and I know each other, but I’ve got a proven record of how to bring people together,” Scalise mentioned ahead of the vote, trying to play up his experience, including more than a decade on the leadership team that included a stint as whip.

As House Republicans trickled out of the candidates’ forum for breaks or to take phone calls, one member, granted anonymity to discuss a private session, stated Scalise and Jordan “both have strong points, but they both have flaws.” Each made an unsuccessful bid for speaker in 2023 after the ouster of Kevin McCarthy, before the gavel ultimately went to Johnson.

Declining to reveal which would get his vote, the member noted: “I won’t talk about a secret vote, but I know who I think is best to lead us.”.

The incoming minority conference also selected other leaders on Tuesday.

Sources indicate that majority Whip Tom Emmer of Minnesota held off a challenge from Texas Rep. August Pfluger to become minority whip in January, despite some grumbling about how tight votes were handled on the floor this year.

“We’ve got to retool our whip operation,” Texas Rep. Nathaniel Moran remarked Tuesday morning, pointing to “the number of times we were held up by either discharge petitions or failed rule votes.”.

“Those were things that should not have happened in the majority,” mentioned Moran as he publicly backed Pfluger for whip.

But Emmer projected confidence after his whip win, comparing the moment to when Republicans were down and out after their losses in 2018 only to rebound a few years later.

“To our colleagues on the left, enjoy this honeymoon phase, because come Jan. 3, 2027, you will regret ever putting your name on a ballot,” he said at a news conference, adding that Republicans under his watch would expose the “empty promises” that Democrats made to voters and push back on what he called their “radical” agenda.

In the day’s only three-way race, conference Chair Lisa McClain of Michigan defeated Reps. Erin Houchin of Indiana and Greg Steube of Florida to keep her spot.

“We had a spirited leadership election. There were important conversations about the future of our conference, and I listened,” McClain remarked at the news conference.

In the race to lead House Republicans’ campaign arm, Rep. Brian Jack of Georgia defeated Rep. Rudy Yakym of Indiana, seen as an up-and-coming Ways and Means Committee member. That means Jack will take on a huge share of the uphill task of selecting candidates and raising funds for the 2028 cycle as he helms the National Republican Congressional Committee.

But most of the attention heading into Tuesday’s closed-door proceedings was on the minority leader race.

Johnson, the outgoing speaker, declined to endorse a candidate but had encouraging words for Jordan after his win. “He’s going to do an excellent job. He’s a good, trusted friend and brother,” he remarked.

Rep. Tom Cole, R-Okla., remarked it was a “tough choice for the conference to make,” but he wasn’t disappointed in the pick. “He was an exceptionally capable chairman of both Oversight and Judiciary. He’s excellent in an interview,” Cole said of Jordan. “He’s got boundless energy and determination.”.

Jordan’s victory means he will form a political and legal tag team with newly installed White House Chief of Staff Stephen Miller in pushing back on a number of investigations House Democrats have planned for President Donald Trump, some of his second-term administration officials and his business-minded family members.

It has been revealed that democrats will have more than 250 seats in the chamber, with a number of races still uncalled. Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries of New York, expected to become the next House speaker, told reporters last week he predicts Democrats will have at least 255 seats when all the ballots have been counted and verification processes have played out.

“It’s a historic majority in the 21st century,” Jeffries told reporters in Washington, D.C., the day after the midterms. “The American people have chosen the economy over extremism. The American people have chosen hope over hatred. The American people have chosen common sense over corruption, chaos and cruelty. The American people have chosen House Democrats because they want to see a dramatic change in direction.”.

Political analysts have predicted an internal battle within the GOP for the direction the party takes over the next two years — and after Trump leaves office in January 2029.

Recent findings suggest that the Institute for Legislative Analysis, a nonprofit organization that advocates to shrink the size and influence of the government, released a vote study assessment on Monday. Its calculations led ILA to endorse Emmer and three fresh faces: Jordan, Steube and Jack.

It has been revealed that “It’s clear many Republican voters feel their representatives in Washington aren’t representing them,” Ryan McGowan, the institute’s CEO, said in a statement. “It will be interesting to see whether House Republicans respond by choosing leaders … whose voting records are much more closely aligned with the party’s conservative base.”.

Recent findings suggest that several GOP sources late last week, granted anonymity to be candid, mentioned they were expecting a close outcome between Scalise and Jordan, adding Emmer was working the phones hard to remain whip. One said having either Scalise or Jordan atop the conference, with the expectation of Emmer staying on as whip, “won’t be much of a change at the top.”.

Sources indicate that the fresh leadership team will take over Jan. 3, when Democrats are expected to, in part, use their large majority to target all things Trump 2.0. The same GOP source said the majority party will “inevitably be pursuing impeachment by August recess despite their disciplined statements to the media pre-election.”.

Trump replied in the affirmative when a “60 Minutes” correspondent asked him in an interview that aired Sunday night if he could work with Democrats, should they also be aggressively investigating his team.

Sources indicate that “Well, I did it for four years,” the president noted of his first term. “They impeached me twice. And there are those that say that worked out to my advantage.”.

Nina Heller, Michael Macagnone and Samantha Freeman contributed to this report.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that A handful of things are non-negotiable at Thanksgiving. You need turkey, stuffing, cranberry sauce, and, of course, a slice of pie to round out your meal. And pumpkin pie is the undeniable star of the dessert table.

In a recent development, but sometimes you're strapped for time and have too much on your plate (pun intended) to whip something up from scratch. So we tried six different grocery store pumpkin pies to find the best store-bought shortcut. And our team's verdict was pretty unanimous, even if it’s a bit hard to hear: No premade pie will ever taste as good as a homemade one.

It has been revealed that it primarily comes down to the crust. Frozen and pre-baked pies typically rely on vegetable-based fat instead of butter because they’re more affordable, reliable, and shelf-stable—but that comes at a cost. You not only miss out on the decadent, buttery taste, but the crusts can also leave an unpleasant film on your tongue.

That said, when you need to outsource to the grocery store, we found two options that will work in a pinch.

Recent findings suggest that the pie that we’d feel most confident bringing to Thanksgiving dinner comes straight from the Whole Foods bakery department. That’s not to say it’s perfect, though. The crust is almost upsettingly pale, but it’s made with real butter and only a little bit of palm oil. And since it doesn’t leave a noticeable film and still lets the butter flavor shine, we’ll let this one slide.

It has been revealed that once you look past the crust’s color, this pie is solid overall. The filling is decadent, not too sweet, and creamy without being mushy. Whole Foods doesn’t shy away from the spices, either.

Senior Editor Samantha MacAvoy noted that the warming spices are nicely balanced, while Designer Alison Dominguez noted, “The flavor was exactly how a pumpkin pie should taste.”.

Costco’s pumpkin pie isn’t perfect: The crust uses palm oil-based shortening rather than butter and can develop a soggy bottom if you buy it too far in advance. (And it doesn’t hold a candle to the warehouse’s holy grail pumpkin cheesecake.) But it has a cult following for a reason, and not just because of its $5.99 price tag.

Even with its faults, the crust has great flavor and enough salt to create a balanced bite. Dominguez appreciated how it was “flaky and not too thick, and most importantly, it let the pie filling itself shine.” News and Features Editor Amanda Mactas chose Costco’s pie as her number one pick. “It all seemed to melt together in one creamy bite,” she stated.

And at over three pounds, this dessert is the indisputable champion if you want to feed a crowd for less.

Our editors and experts handpick every product we feature. We may earn a commission from your purchases.Learn more.

October through December is a magical time at the supermarket, when the aisles transform into a treasure trove of new foods for the holidays. It’s all of our favorite snacks, but in the coziest seasonal flavors.

We’re on a mission to discover the hottest new groceries all year long, so when seasonal and limited-time items hit the shelves, you know we’re stocking up on the best of the best.

From stuffing-inspired potato chips to fizzy cranberry drinks, these are the holiday items worth seeking out the next time you’re at the grocery store.

In a recent development, “A hill I will die on? Cranberry is the best fall flavor. This soda has the fresh, fizzy bubbles I’ve come to expect from lemon-lime Poppi—but with a subtle twist. The cranberry flavor hits you on the back end of your palate and adds a subtle twang to a standard white soda. Cranberry Fizz Poppi is ideal for sipping on its own or pairing with cranberry juice for a more prominent flavor.” —Katie Bandurski, deputy shopping editor.

Recent findings suggest that “Disclaimer: Peppermint is not normally my holiday flavor of choice. I’m much more into the eggnog and gingerbread of it all. But when Sprouts came out with a latest peppermint chocolate version of its famous Gluten-Free coconut rolls, I had to look past my ‘won’t this just taste like eating a candy cane?’ aversion. It turns out that Sprouts found just the right balance of mint, bitter dark chocolate and just-sweet enough coconut milk—three flavors that I still can’t believe work this well together.

Texturally, these coconut rolls are outstanding. The light, crispy rolls, coated in snappy chocolate and crunchy snowflake sprinkles, are so easy to eat that I finished the entire bag in two days.” —Val Goodrich, food writer.

“I grabbed these stuffing-flavored kettle chips at the Trader Joe’s checkout line last week, and I need to go back to buy about 10 more bags. There’s something about the salty, crunchy kettle chips paired with the spot-on flavorings of herby stuffing that make these THE fall snack. The notes of sage and thyme come through in every bite without being overpowering.” —KB.

“I like to prep homemade pistachio milk and pistachio syrup for my iced lattes in the morning on a semi-regular basis, but somehow I never thought to use pistachio milk to make a peppermint mocha. Tache’s fresh peppermint mocha pistachio milk means that I can have a pepperminty, decadent and rich iced pistachio peppermint mocha with just a carton and espresso—no time-consuming homemade syrups or sauces necessary.

This milk is made for putting in coffee, but I’ll even drink it plain, without any added espresso, because it’s just that good. Tache also recommends shaking it with espresso and vodka to make an espresso martini, which sounds like a perfect holiday cocktail. —Lauren Pahmeier, editor.

Industry observers note that “Casting my love of the Great British Baking Show aside, where someone is always rolling out rough puff and traditional puff, everyone knows buying puff pastry versus making it from scratch is a clutch move. Especially during the holidays when there are so many other things to make.

Trader Joe’s all-butter puff pastry version is only available during the fall and winter months and it flies off the shelves, so I always stock up and buy several boxes at a time. It’s the best all-butter frozen puff pastry for the price (two rectangle sheets for less than $6!), and it doesn’t have any fillers or preservatives. It tastes great, puffs nicely and can be used for on-the-fly appetizers and pretty desserts when manufacturer drops in.” —Lesley Balla, editor.

“Pretzels and apple pie aren’t really something I would have pictured as a pair. But when I discovered this unique combination at a food show last year, I knew I had to take a bag of Pop Daddy’s Dutch Apple Pie Seasoned Pretzels home with me. The apple flavor combined with the cinnamon-sugar coating makes me think of messy apple cider doughnuts. The apple pie pretzels are my top choice but I love Pop Daddy’s gluten-free tomato basil pretzels and smoked Gouda pretzels, too.” —LP.

In a recent development, “I love a good pistachio ice cream, and this pistachio macaron-inspired option from Jeni’s has it all. It’s sweet, salty and nutty, with an unforgettable texture that captures the chewiness of a macaron. The slight almond flavor complements the other ingredients without being overpowering. I also like the natural hue of this ice cream rather than the bright green often associated with pistachio ice cream.” —KB.

“I don’t say this lightly, but Haymaker Bun Tech giant’s sticky buns might actually rival my mom’s Christmas morning cinnamon rolls. (Sorry, Mom.) I made them for my family on a rainy Saturday morning and they were spectacular. The buttery brioche is impossibly soft, with generous swirls of cinnamon and all the sticky, gooey goodness you want from a cinnamon roll. They’re made in Vermont, shipped frozen and ready after just 15 minutes in the oven, which seems like an almost unreasonable amount of convenience for something so delicious. I’m already trying to justify keeping a permanent supply in my freezer.” —Lindsay Parill, trends writer.

It has been revealed that “They say the cheese is supposed to be the star of a cheese board, but these Trader Joe’s crackers give any wedge some serious competition. They’re thin with a crisp like a crouton and speckled with dried mission figs, briny kalamata olives, and a mix of seeds for a balance of sweet, savory and hearty.

Aperitivo (aka snacking before dinner) is sacred in my house, and my go-to is a circle of these crisps surrounding a bowl of whipped ricotta with sea salt and a drizzle of good balsamic. On a full cheese or charcuterie board, I’ll pair them with pretty much any soft or spreadable cheese, plus fig jam, honey and halved grapes. Buy an extra box—they’ll disappear rapidly!” —Rachel Vigoda, senior deputy editor.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recipe by Susan Bronson, Rhinelander, Wisconsin.

Tested by Taste of Home Test Kitchen.

Taste of Home's Editorial Process.

Dirty rice has met its noodle match with our Louisiana-style dirty spaghetti.

Let the good times roll with this Louisiana-inspired dirty spaghetti dish! It’s a riff on Cajun-Creole dirty rice that transforms the original into an easy one-pot pasta.

According to recent reports, the key it its flavor is Cajun seasoning, a blend cayenne pepper, garlic powder, black pepper, paprika and thyme. And herein lies an important cooking tip: When using store-bought seasoning blends like this one, give them a little taste first before adding anything to the pot. Different brands rely on different ratios of ingredients, and a tablespoon of one product could be much milder (or pack way more heat!) than a tablespoon of another. Your personal preferences matter, too. So whether you are sensitive to spice or like to pack on the heat, make sure you’re adding the proper amount of spice for your taste.

According to recent reports, dirty spaghetti is a riff on dirty rice, a classic Cajun-Creole side dish. Traditional dirty rice is made with chopped organ meats such as chicken livers or gizzards, which, along with the herbs and seasonings, color the white rice and earn it its “dirty” moniker. This dish, however, has a meaty base that’s made with ground beef and diced andouille sausage. Like the original, it also features the “holy trinity” of Cajun and Creole cooking: chopped onion, bell pepper and celery. A healthy dose of Cajun seasoning ensures each bite is packed with bold flavor.

It has been revealed that heat the oil in a large Dutch oven or large high-sided skillet over medium-high heat. Add the ground beef and cook it until it’s browned, four to six minutes, using a wooden spoon or spatula to break it into small crumbles.

Editor’s Tip: If you use a skillet, make sure it has a lid.

Add the chopped andouille sausage, onion, celery, red pepper and green pepper. Cook them until the vegetables are soft, about three to four minutes. Add the garlic and cook it until it’s fragrant, 30 to 60 seconds. Stir in the tomato paste and Cajun seasoning, and cook for one to two more minutes. Add 3 cups of broth and bring the mixture to a simmer.

Add the broken spaghetti to the pot, ensuring that the noodles are submerged in the liquid and separated as much as possible. Add more liquid if needed. Bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce the heat to medium-low. Cover the pot and simmer the pasta for six minutes.

Sources indicate that remove the lid and continue simmering until the spaghetti is al dente, stirring every two to three minutes. Add more broth as needed. Remove the pot from the heat, and season the pasta to taste with salt and pepper.

Leftover dirty spaghetti can be stored in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to four days.

The best way to reheat a pasta dish like this one is either in the oven or on the stovetop. To reheat leftover dirty spaghetti in the oven, transfer it to an oven-safe baking dish, cover it tightly with foil, and cook it in an oven preheated to 350 degrees for about 20 minutes or until it’s heated through. To reheat it on the stovetop, heat a saucepan over medium heat and add a drizzle of olive oil. Add the leftover pasta and sauce and saute them for about two to three minutes or until they’re hot.

Sources indicate that yes, you can freeze dirty spaghetti. After allowing it to cool completely, transfer leftovers to a freezer-safe container and store them in the freezer for up to three months. Allow the dirty spaghetti to thaw overnight in the fridge before reheating it.

The best pan for making this one-pot pasta dish is a Dutch oven or a large, high-walled skillet or pot with a tight-fitting lid.

Sources indicate that first, be sure to give your Cajun seasoning a little taste first because seasoning blends like this one can vary widely in spiciness. Depending on how spicy your Cajun seasoning is, add more or less to taste. You could also make a homemade Cajun seasoning blend and customize the amount of cayenne pepper and chili powder to your personal taste. The andouille sausage also adds quite a bit of spice; for less heat, skip it entirely, or swap in sweet Italian sausage, breakfast sausage, chicken sausage or a milder smoked sausage like kielbasa.

You’ll definitely want to pair this dirty spaghetti with crusty French bread, garlic bread or cornbread to sop up any extra sauce. Southern-inspired side dishes to consider include southern green beans, collard greens or black-eyed pea tomato salad. Or, complement the pasta dish’s spicy flavor with a fresh and crisp green salad.
